body: @nicorikken - the two links to example projects go to pages that list a bunch of projects - is the implication that all of those listed are under this license?

# New submission review

## Definitive Factors

_These must all be satisfied to allow inclusion in the license list_

1. **Is the submitted license unique, that is, it does not match another license already on the License List as per the [matching guidelines](https://spdx.org/spdx-license-list/matching-guidelines)?**
    - [x] Yes
    - [ ] No
1. **If a software license, does it apply to source code and not only to executables?**
    - [x] Yes - not entirely clear, but nothing prevents it from being applicable to source code
    - [ ] No
1. **Does the license have identifiable and stable text, and is not in the midst of drafting?**
    - [x] Yes - appears so
    - [ ] No
1. **Has the license steward, if any, committed to versioning new versions and to not modify it after addition to the list?**
    - [x] Yes - appears so
    - [ ] No

## Other factors for inclusion

*Roughly in order of descending importance*

1. **Does the license substantially comply with one of the free/open content definitions? (examples include the [Open Source Definition](https://opensource.org/osd) and the [Debian Free Software Guidelines](https://www.debian.org/social_contract#guidelines))** (_Approval by the organisation that publishes the definition is not required_)
    - [ ] Yes 
    - [x] No - no, there is a restriction on modifications, "The software license extends to modifications permitted under the relevant IEC standard. "
1. **Is the license structured to be generally usable by anyone, and not specific to one organisation or project?**
    - [ ] Yes
    - [x] No - really only relevant for code ("Code Components") related to IEC standards
1. **Does the license have substantial use such that it is likely to be encountered (ie. use in many projects, or in one significant project)?** (_For recently written licenses, definitive plans for it to be used in at least one or a few significant projects may satisfy this_)
    - unclear at this point
1. **Is the license primarily intended to facilitate the free distribution of content with limited restrictions?**
    - [x] Yes - I would say so, even though it has a restriction on types of modification
    - [ ] No
1. **Does the license steward support this submission, or is at least aware of and not in opposition of it?**
    - unknown - @nicorikken - do you know or do you work for IEC?

## Summary of factors, outcome, comments
I'm mostly +1 to add, but would like to have an update on usage before making a final decision

I agree with @jlovejoy's comments above, writing here to add a few additional thoughts:
* I'm also overall +1 to add
* I'd note that the CoMPAS project that @nicorikken is part of the Linux Foundation's [LF Energy family of projects](https://www.lfenergy.org/projects/compas/), noting just as relevant to "Other factor" 3 for significance of a project where the license is being used
* If this does get added, I would however _not_ want to use the identifier `CC-EULA` for this. I think we've been fairly consistent in only using `CC` as the _starting prefix_ for Creative Commons licenses (some other licenses or exceptions may include `CC`, but I don't think as a prefix).

When I saw this issue titled `CC-EULA` my first assumption was that this would be Creative Commons-related, so I'd suggest we go instead with e.g. `IEC-Code-Components-EULA` since it really is specific to this particular work.

@swinslow thanks for filling in while I was away. Indeed the SCD files are used to generate the code API related code. The 1:1 copy of the files is stored in https://github.com/com-pas/compas-scl-xsd with some wrapper to publish as a module.

This module is imported into the compas-core project: https://github.com/com-pas/compas-core/blob/0fa667cf07bd8665cf048b82228ebd663926f12f/pom.xml#L74-L78 and amended with some custom definitions, as described in the architecture documentation https://github.com/com-pas/compas-architecture/blob/main/technical/XSD_EXTENSIONS.md

The OpenSCD project is another project (also used inside of the CoMPAS project) https://github.com/openscd which also uses these XSD files and so is bound to the same IEC license.

All so-called 'code components' that are distributed as additions to the standard are distributed by IEC under the terms of this CC-EULA license. Some of those code components are available here: https://www.iec.ch/dyn/www/f?p=103:227:4631044159258::::FSP_ORG_ID,FSP_LANG_ID:1273,25 As you can tell it is quite some code there. It is likely that some parts of the standard will be added to the code components in the near future as well, as some trivial but essential pieces of code are not yet distributed in this way.

As this is a niche license for which there is little legal consensus, we have chosen not to include the code directly into the main repository, which is why you mainly see Apache 2.0 licensed code.

Regarding the identifier, IEC uses CC-EULA but indeed I too thought of Creative Commons when I first encountered it :smile: So I'm fine with changing it to something more meaningful. 

I have informed IEC in the past about the intention to submit it to SPDX, but that has been a while ago. Also communication with IEC about this license has been confusing at times. So now that there is a concrete request I'll inform them about it.

Thanks @nicorikken! Appreciate the additional context and feedback here, that is all helpful to know.

Given the comments, I'm a firmer +1 to add, though I'd suggest we leave this pending for a week or so in order to see whether anyone from IEC decides to weigh in (as the license author / "steward"). If we don't hear back from them, I'd be in favor of adding unless there are objections to be discussed.
@jlovejoy You mentioned in your original writeup that you were "mostly +1 to add, but would like to have an update on usage before making a final decision" -- are you good to give a +1 now?
